title: Anyone having issues with unity editor using insane amounts of RAM?
author: Upstairs_Tone_4227
selftext:
I am using Opus 5.5 on high as my orchestrator with a few sub-agents to build an open world forest scene. At the start of the day unity editor is only using a few GB of RAM. But by the end of the day, it can get as high as 15GB RAM. It seems to accumulate overtime the longer the AI works in a scene. The only solution I’ve found is to have the agents restart the editor periodically to lower RAM usage.

Does anyone have any advice on how to keep RAM from increasing over time whether it’s something in Unity or a change in how the agents work?

comments.author: Outrageous-Issue9722
comments.body: You're not going to like this answer probably but... 15gb really isn't a lot for game dev.  Game dev, especially 3d, and especially detailed 3d use a lot of ram, and the editor usually has to have all it most of it loaded at once.

replies.author: Upstairs_Tone_4227
replies.body: Thanks I’ll check those. I mainly wanted to see if it’s normal for RAM to 3x during a session. I’m at 48GB ram right now and wanted to run 3-4 unity editor sessions at once but I’m now not sure if it’s that’s gonna be possible.

replies.author: Outrageous-Issue9722
replies.body: You can do it.  Make an empty scene that is the "default" scene so when you open the editor it loads that one.  When using AI, have them do their work from there.  Once you start loading scenes with assets/etc in them, ram will go up.  For the open world aspect, look into asset streaming/bundles so you can develop areas in pieces/batches instead of having the whole world loaded.

replies.author: UsernameUsed
replies.body: I've been watching Jason weimann on YouTube, he's a long time unity game dev, and I believe that he said he doesnt even open the editor ( maybe just for testing, idk) and just has opus use the unity cli and write unity files directly. If i find the video he said it in ill post a link.

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body: “Open world” sounds like a good way to eat RAM, nom nom nom.

comments.author: UnderLord7985
comments.body: No thats about what mine uses when im using chatgpt astra to help me code my game. Its becsuse of all the unity handlers and the more stuff you put in the more you'll use, iv had unity upto 20gigs of ram so far on my 32gb comp

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body:
Do you know how to make games without AI? If not, you probably skipped the chapter on optimization.   
Just throw more RAM at the problem and all will be solved..?

replies.author: Upstairs_Tone_4227
replies.body: I’ve never made an open world game without AI help, no. I have been focusing on optimization periodically though. Game is running at 100 FPS on an old rtx 3060 GPU.

comments.author: sm0ke_rings
comments.body: Your agent can use unity headless, but it's likely to come at the cost of tokens.
